Explain or produce the answer independently rather than relying only on recognition.
Apply the idea accurately to a new prompt and check every required detail.
mustMemoriseRules: rates-practical hypothesis → a testable prediction about concentration and rate explained using collision theory
gas-syringe method → measuring gas volume produced over time as concentration changes
turbidity method → timing a colour or cloudiness change such as a cross becoming obscured
rates dependent variable → rate, gas volume over time or time to a fixed endpoint
rates control variables → temperature, total volume where appropriate, other reactant amounts, apparatus and endpoint method
steeper product-time gradient → evidence of a faster reaction rate
product-time plateau → the stage when the limiting reactant has been used up and no more product forms
instantaneous rate → rate estimated from the gradient of a tangent at one point on a curve
repeatability → similar results obtained by the same person using the same method and equipment
